'''''Erica tetralix''''', the '''cross-leaved heath''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Ericaceae]], [[Native species|native]] to western Europe.

== Description ==
It is a [[perennial]] [[subshrub]] with glandular [[leaves]] in [[Whorl (botany)|whorls]] of four (whence the name). Appearing in summer and autumn, small pink bell-shaped [[flower]]s droop in compact clusters at the ends of the shoots.

=== Similar species ===
Related species ''[[Erica cinerea|E. cinerea]]'' has glabrous leaves in whorls of three. ''[[Calluna vulgaris]]'' has much smaller and scale-like leaves in opposite and [[decussate]] pairs.<ref name="Stace">{{cite book|author=Clive Stace|author-link=Clive Stace |year=2010|title=New Flora of the British Isles|edition=3rd|publisher=Cambridge University Press}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
The sticky, adhesive glands on leaves, sepals and other parts of the plant prompted [[Charles Darwin]] to suggest that this species might be a [[protocarnivorous plant]], but little, if any, research has been done on this.<ref name="Darwin 1875">{{cite book|author=Darwin, Charles|author-link=Charles Robert Darwin |year=1875|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=I-JG1PqzMrEC|title=Insectivorous Plants|location=London|publisher=J. Murray}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''E. tetralix'' is [[Native species|native]] to western Europe from southern [[Portugal]] to central [[Norway]], as well as a number of boggy regions further from the coast in Central Europe such as [[Austria]] and [[Switzerland]]. It has also been [[Introduced species|introduced]] to parts of North America.

''E. tetralix'' can become a dominant part of the [[flora]] in [[bog]]s, wet [[heath]]s, and damp [[conifer]]ous woodland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://linnaeus.nrm.se/flora/di/erica/erica/erictetv.jpg|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20051122131839/http://linnaeus.nrm.se/flora/di/erica/erica/erictetv.jpg|archive-date=2005-11-22|title=Distribution map (polar view)|website=Linne's Webbplatz|publisher=Swedish Museum of Natural History}}</ref>

== Ecology ==
A species of ''[[Trialeurodes]]'' whitefly discovered in 1971 was named ''T. ericae'' for the plant, due to its frequent association with it.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Bink-Moenen |first=Rosita M. |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/57850816#page/29/mode/1up |journal=Entomologische Berichten |date=1 February 1976 |volume=36 |issue=2 |location=Amsterdam |pages=17 |title=A new whitefly of ''Erica tetralix: Trialeurodes ericae'' sp. n. (Homoptera, Aleyrodidae)}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
In cultivation, like other heathers, ''E. tetralix'' requires an [[acidic soil]], as it is a [[calcifuge]]. Numerous [[cultivar]]s have been developed for garden use, of which ''E. tetralix'' [[form (botany)|f.]] ''alba'' 'Alba Mollis'<ref>{{cite web|title=''Erica tetralix'' f. ''alba'' 'Alba Mollis'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/94077/Erica-tetralix-f-alba-Alba-Mollis/Details|publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|access-date=8 June 2020}}</ref> (a white-flowered variety) and ''E. tetralix'' f. ''stellata'' 'Pink Star'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/97870/Erica-tetralix-f-stellata-Pink-Star/Details | title = ''Erica tetralix'' f. ''stellata'' 'Pink Star' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 8 June 2020}}</ref> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 36 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 6 February 2018}}</ref>

== In culture ==
It appears in the 1938 German marching song "[[Erika (song)|Erika]]" by [[Herms Niel]].
